body:
Summer 2023

A $300,000 Odyssey Award from the Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation provides critical resources to develop a groundbreaking platform to analyze the structure and function of disordered proteins that drive disease progression. This pioneering project promises to reveal structural biological insights while validating a powerful new tool to inform drug discovery across multiple cancers.

title: A Celebration for the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber
body:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Justin Knight

Supporters gathered to celebrate the recently established Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber. The endowed Chair was funded by colleagues, mentees, grateful patients, family, and friends in honor of Robert J. Mayer, MD, who served as director of the Fellowship Program for more than 35 years. Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, who succeeded Mayer as director, was appointed the first incumbent. Pictured (from left): Mayer, LaCasce, and Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD.

title: Holiday Patient Assistance
body:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan

The Holiday Patient Assistance Program, which helps patients and families in critical financial need, raised $192,785 in 2022. The program helped 726 eligible Dana-Farber patients and families celebrate the season by providing gift cards to help cover the cost of expenses like gas to travel to appointments, groceries for holiday meals, and small gifts for loved ones.

title: Jog for Julie
body:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Jessamyn Martin

The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber.

body:
Spring 2023
By Colleen Sullivan
Photography by Capehart Photography 

Institute Trustee Michele Kessler and her husband, Howard Kessler, made a gift of $250,000 to launch the Cannabis Care Support Program at Dana-Farber, which aims to create sustainable oncologic cannabis educational resources and advance research on the use of cannabis to address the mental and physical side effects of cancer.
